title: Iman Gadzhi at 18: hunger, social circle, self-education and LTV-based agency selling
summary: Early interview with Iman at 18 on how poverty-driven hunger, a guarded social circle and relentless self-education built his agency and personal brand. He also explains how to sell social media marketing by anchoring on client lifetime value, niche research and emotional motives instead of flat retainers.

principles.text: Start with whatever motivation lights a fire (fear, proving people wrong). A deeper purpose comes later as you grow.
principles.quote: start off with the thing that just lights a fire under us and then certainly you know as you go through the paradigms you'll realize that what really matters

principles.text: Your social circle shapes you. Take advice only from people who have what you want and limit time with those who don't move forward.
principles.quote: I don't take fitness advice from people who don't have the body I want

principles.text: Successful people talk about solutions. Peers who speculate about hypotheticals are worth phasing out.
principles.quote: the people people who are successful when they sit around a table they talk about solutions right they talk about solutions and how they're going to do something

principles.text: Self-education is free to start: read used books and use the internet instead of waiting for a paid course.
principles.quote: go to a used book store go online the Internet's free right like like you have internet at home start now

principles.text: Sell marketing off the client's lifetime value, not a flat retainer, so the ROI math makes the price obvious.
principles.quote: what I always start off with especially if I'm selling paid traffic LTV lifetime value so I need to first off figure out what is the lifetime value of a customer

principles.text: Do niche research (best-converting ads, industry LTV) so you know the industry better than the owner and flip the buyer-seller authority dynamic.
principles.quote: know the industry better than the business owner does start off what no one talks about this I don't hear anyone talking about this niche research
